title: How do you actually handle money?
intro: Not how you think you handle it. The read is on what you do when a number is in front of you, which is usually different.
og_line: Six questions on what you actually do when a number is in front of you.

cta.title: The calculators
cta.label: Open the calculators
cta.blurb: Rate, break even, pricing and startup cost. The four numbers most of this comes down to, worked out rather than guessed.

options.a: I say a number and stop talking
I say a number slightly lower than I meant to
I ask what their budget is first
I go high. They can always say no
It stays there
It goes into the thing I have been putting off buying
It gets absorbed and I could not tell you where
It goes against the next known cost

questions.q: How often do you look at what you actually made last month?

options.a: Monthly, in a spreadsheet I built
When something feels wrong
Constantly. I know the balance right now
I look at revenue, not profit
I have modelled exactly who I would lose
Makes me feel sick
Already did it. They paid
I would need to check what I charge now

questions.q: Spending on something that might not work:

options.a: Fine, if the downside is survivable
Only with a number on the return
Almost never. That is how money disappears
I would rather not think about it

questions.q: The money mistake you have actually made:

options.a: Charged too little for too long
Sat on cash while the moment passed
Bet on something before it was proven
Did not look until it was a problem

results.name: The Underpricer
results.headline: You charge what feels polite rather than what the work is worth.
results.body: You would rather be busy than paid, and you find out too late that the cheapest supplier attracts the hardest customers.
results.cost: You will work twice as hard for the same money, and resent the client for a price you set.

results.name: The Hoarder
results.headline: Nothing leaves the account without a fight.
results.body: Cash in the bank is the only number you trust, which makes you very hard to kill and slightly hard to grow.
results.cost: The thing you would not spend on was sometimes the thing that would have worked.

results.name: The Big Swinger
results.headline: You would rather bet it than sit on it.
results.body: You size a decision by what it could return rather than what it could cost, which is why your good years are very good.
results.cost: One bad quarter lands harder on you than on anybody else, because there is no float behind it.

results.name: The Avoider
results.headline: The numbers exist. You have not looked at them.
results.body: It is not that you cannot do the maths. It is that knowing makes it real, so the spreadsheet stays closed and the decisions get made on vibes.
results.cost: Every problem you find late costs more than the same problem found early.

results.name: The Engineer
results.headline: You priced it off the numbers and you can show your working.
results.body: You know your margin, your break even and what an hour of your time costs, which puts you ahead of most people running a business.
results.cost: A model can talk you out of a good decision that the numbers cannot see yet.
